Power comparison of the filters on simulated series

Source: R/simulate.R
fmhp_simulation.Rd

fmhp_simulation() repeats the simulation study of Hanif, Iqbal and Choudhary (2017, Tables 1 and 2): for each design it simulates series with mhp_simulate(), filters them with the HP, modified HP and fully modified HP filters, and compares the root mean square error of the estimated cycles against the true one, over the whole series, its middle and its ends.

Usage

fmhp_simulation(
  designs = mhp_designs(),
  n_rep = 100L,
  T = 200L,
  trend = c("linear", "nonlinear"),
  aggregate = c("none", "systematic", "sum", "average"),
  lambda = NULL,
  max_lambda = 3000L,
  seed = NULL,
  form = c("rows", "differences")
)

Arguments

designs

designs as in mhp_designs() (default: all 30).

n_rep

replicates per design (default 100; the paper used 1000).

T

number of quarterly observations (default 200).

trend, aggregate

as in mhp_simulate().

lambda

the HP smoothing parameter (default NULL: 1600, or 100 for aggregated series).

max_lambda

the largest \(\lambda\) of the searches (default 3000).

seed

seed of the random numbers (NULL: the current state).

form

the form of the end-point weights of the fully modified HP filter (default "rows"); see fmhp_filter().

Value

An object of class c("mhp_simulation", "mhp_result", "list"): rmse (a data.table with one row per design and filter: model, sd_ratio, ar1, ar2, method, rmse, rmse_middle, rmse_ends), power (one row per design: the share of replicates in which FMHP beats HP and MHP) and settings. plot() draws the RMSE by design.

Details

The RMSE of a filter is \(\{T^{-1}\sum_t(\hat{c}_t - c_t)^2\}^{1/2}\); the middle is the central 80% of the observations and the ends the first and last 10%. fmhp_better is the share of replicates in which the FMHP filter has a smaller RMSE than the HP filter (Table 1 of the paper reports it in percent). The series are filtered on their own scale (log_scale = FALSE).

References

Hanif, M. N., Iqbal, J. and Choudhary, M. A. (2017). Fully modified HP filter. SBP Working Paper Series, No. 88, State Bank of Pakistan.

See also

mhp_simulate, fmhp_filter

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

sim <-
  fmhp_simulation(
      designs    = mhp_designs()[c(3, 13, 23)]
    , n_rep      = 2
    , T          = 120
    , trend      = "linear"
    , aggregate  = "none"
    , lambda     = NULL
    , max_lambda = 3000
    , seed       = 1
    , form       = "rows"
    )
sim$power
#> Key: <model>
#>    model sd_ratio   ar1   ar2 fmhp_better_hp fmhp_better_mhp
#>    <int>    <num> <num> <num>          <num>           <num>
#> 1:     3     10.0   1.2  -0.4            0.0             0.0
#> 2:    13      2.0   1.2  -0.4            1.0             0.5
#> 3:    23      0.5   1.2  -0.4            0.5             0.5
